comment: Blast-radius map for the CI fast tier (ADR 0170). scripts/ci-plan.py reads it.
Each changed path collects the areas of every rule whose pattern matches it; the fast tier
runs the union. '**' matches across directories, '*' within one path segment.
'@native-fixture-sources' stands for the sources of every executable the full tier's
X11 1x lines run. ci-plan.py also adds one rule per slow group: the sources of its tests
(from CMakeLists.txt) select the group, so changing a slow test runs it.
A path that matches no rule selects the fallback areas, and 'ci-plan.py check' fails
until a rule covers it. The area 'full' switches the run to the full tier; 'job:<id>' adds that full-tier job.
The full tier ignores this map and runs everything.

areas.build: Build everything (ci-fast preset), run CTest except unselected slow tests, and the repository checks.
areas.native: The X11 1x native display tests (the full tier's 'Native tests: X11 1x' lines), in parallel.
areas.slow-core: Slow core geometry and document CTest suites.
areas.full: Run the full tier: the path is a harness most full-tier jobs share.
areas.job:audit: Run the full tier's 'Native tests: audit and accessibility' job (with the development build).
areas.job:fractional: Run the full tier's fractional-scaling, Blender worker and M5 job (with the development build).
areas.job:sanitize: Run the full tier's 'Sanitized builds' job.
areas.job:ifc: Run the 'IFC library and helper' job (ADR 0171): IfcOpenShell prefix, sketchyup-ifc-worker, the API probe and the packaging checks. The fast tier restores the cached prefix; the full tier builds it from source.
areas.job:skp: Run the 'SKP parser, helper and import' job (ADR 0176): the vendored OpenSKP parser subset checked against its pinned archives, sketchyup-skp-worker, and the application's import and package tests.

rules.why: Prose only. Nothing builds or reads these.
Published schemas and the generated reference: tests read them and the fast tier checks them against the live registries.

Core geometry and document model: everything builds and the native tests run; the slow core suites run too. The slow terrain and provider suites wait for their own paths or the full tier. third_party/ifcopenshell is not here: only sketchyup-ifc-worker links it (rule below).
Application, automation, I/O and integration code.

IFC (ADR 0171): the vendored IfcOpenShell tree, the helper that links it, its API probe, fixtures and library checks, and the files that pin and describe it. The application does not link the library, so the vendored tree alone selects only the IFC job, which restores the cached prefix (the tree and src/ifc/IfcOpenShellPrefix.cmake key the cache); src, scripts and tests paths also select build and native through the generic rules. The root CMakeLists.txt is here too (R097.b): it defines the SKETCHYUP_BUILD_IFC option and adds src/ifc, so an edit there can break the helper build, and the job costs about a minute with the prefix cached.

SKP (ADR 0176): the vendored OpenSKP parser subset, the helper that links it, the package decoder, the synthetic fixtures and the files that pin and describe it. The application does not link the parser, so the vendored tree alone selects only the SKP job (a plain C++17 build, a few minutes); src, scripts and tests paths also select build and native through the generic rules.

R109 S3 and S4 (ADR 0183): the sandbox of the text helper and the extension worker, their policies, the helpers' host code and the suites that run them. The sanitized builds run both helpers and their suites under ASan and UBSan.
Build definition: build and run everything fast, native included.

Native document schema (R099.a, ADR 0173; R100.a, ADR 0174): schema 30 with presentation-v1, schema 31 with edge-styles-v1, the record decoders and the .sketchystyle envelope. A format change runs the full tier, including the package acceptance's prior-release check and the Qt 6.8 compile.
Terrain code and suites select the slow terrain suites.
Assistant and provider code selects the provider release corpus.

R100.c (ADR 0174 sections 4, 5 and 10): the .sketchycat catalog format on the shared envelope, its decoder, its fuzz determinism test and its generated fixtures. The generic source and test rules already select build and native; this rule names the slice.

R100.d (ADR 0174 sections 4, 5 and 7): the catalog library reference, catalog.import, catalog.export and their refusal, relocation, appearance and save checks. The generic source and test rules already select build and native; this rule names the slice.

R100.e (ADR 0174 sections 7 and 10): the style and catalog CLI flags, their refusals, the --capabilities and --describe-command shapes and the library export. The generic source and test rules already select build and native; this rule names the slice.

R100.b (ADR 0174 Q1): the textured material presets, their generated textures and embedded CC0 files, and the Poly Haven notice. The Textured group of the Materials library is tested by material_input_tests, which the build and native lines run.

R100.f1 (ADR 0174 section 10, UX_DESIGN §18.3): the edge stroke's viewport drawing (dash runs, opacity, texture tiling and the missing-texture hatch), its status chip and the document.style edits. The generic source and test rules already select build and native; this rule names the slice.
Test sources, fixtures and helpers run by CTest or the repository checks.
Native display fixtures and the headers they share.

The R100.f3 Asset catalogs dialog (UX_DESIGN 18.5 to 18.7) and its missing-dependency report, the Export asset catalog dialog (18.1, 18.6) and the File menu flow, with the input suite that drives them and the native display lines that run it. The suite links the desktop, so it runs in the fast tier as well.

The R099.d2 Presentations dialog (UX_DESIGN 17): the dialog, its scene picker and the Camera menu entry, with the input suite that drives them and the native display lines that run it. The suite links the desktop, so it runs in the fast tier as well.

R101.e2 (UX_DESIGN section 19): the Quantities section of the Model Tray, its off-thread runs, schedules and exports, driven through the main window offscreen and on the native display lines. Its dialogs are in the native dialog audit's quantities group.

The R097.e1 import screens suite (ADR 0171), its R098.a3 STEP twin (ADR 0172), the R102.c SketchUp twin (ADR 0176) the R097.e2 export screens suite (ADR 0171) and its R098.c2 STEP export twin (ADR 0172 section 8): the options dialog, the progress sheet, the report and the refusal and unavailable sheets, offscreen and driven by a stand-in helper. They link the desktop but not the IFC library, so they run in the fast tier (build and the native display lines) as well as the IFC job the generic IFC rule selects.
Glb, texture, section and smooth exports and the render integrations are what the Blender job verifies.
Scripts the fast tier runs: test wrappers, verifiers and generators.
Packaging and release scripts are what the package job verifies.
The pinned mirror decides every CI package, so everything conditional runs.
CI definition: rerun the fast tier on itself. The plan job always checks the inventory and this map.
Exporter inputs the Blender verifiers check: sections, textures, materials, smoothing and solar.
Desktop entry, MIME, icons and the bundled assemblies are validated by the package job.
Fixtures native tests read as well as CTest.
Harnesses most full-tier jobs share (the Wayland runner, the build-tree packing): run the full tier.
Harnesses one full-tier job runs: that job (and the development build it needs) runs in the fast tier.
M5 offline acceptance runs in the fractional-scaling job.
The private Wayland client fix is built and checked by the sanitize job.

examples.why: IFC helper source and its probe test (R097.a)
root CMakeLists.txt alone selects the IFC job (R097.b; R097.a left it out)

test_seconds.comment: Serial seconds in the development build on a CI runner (run 39664036473, 2026-10-21). scripts/ci-ctest-shard.py balances the fast tier's CTest shards with them; an unlisted test counts as 1 s. Approximate is fine: it only affects balance.
